{
  "findings": [
    {
      "file": "pkg/storage/unified/search/bleve.go",
      "line": 72,
      "severity": "high",
      "category": "concurrency",
      "title": "Concurrent BuildIndex for the same key can cause file index creation errors",
      "body": "Removing the global cacheMu.Lock from BuildIndex means two goroutines can now concurrently build an index for the same NamespacedResource. getOrCreateIndex does not provide per-key mutual exclusion (see TODO at resource/search.go lines 288-290), so concurrent search requests for the same resource will both see a nil index and call BuildIndex. For file-based indexes (size > FileThreshold), both goroutines will call bleve.New on the same directory path, which is not safe and can fail with an error such as 'index already exists' or corrupt the index. For memory indexes, both will build identical indexes and the last insertion wins, wasting work. Need per-key locking or singleflight to prevent duplicate concurrent builds."
    },
    {
      "file": "pkg/storage/unified/search/bleve.go",
      "line": 145,
      "severity": "high",
      "category": "concurrency",
      "title": "TotalDocs reads the cache map without holding RLock",
      "body": "TotalDocs iterates over b.cache without acquiring b.cacheMu.RLock. With the reduced locking in BuildIndex, cache is now written concurrently by any call to BuildIndex (e.g., from getOrCreateIndex on search requests) while TotalDocs may be called (for example, in searchSupport.init at resource/search.go line 216 or externally). This constitutes a concurrent map read/write and will cause a runtime panic or map corruption. TotalDocs must take cacheMu.RLock, or the cache must be otherwise synchronized."
    },
    {
      "file": "pkg/storage/unified/resource/server.go",
      "line": 258,
      "severity": "medium",
      "category": "bug",
      "title": "Cancel function not called when Init fails during NewResourceServer",
      "body": "NewResourceServer creates a cancellable context and stores its cancel function in the server struct. If s.Init(ctx) returns an error, the function logs and returns nil, err without calling s.cancel(). Any goroutines started during Init (e.g., from lifecycle.Init or WatchWriteEvents in search.init) may continue running with no way to be stopped, leaking resources. The cancel should be invoked before returning the error."
    },
    {
      "file": "pkg/storage/unified/resource/search.go",
      "line": 189,
      "severity": "medium",
      "category": "concurrency",
      "title": "Data race on totalBatchesIndexed in concurrent errgroup goroutines",
      "body": "Inside s.init, totalBatchesIndexed++ is executed by multiple goroutines running under an errgroup with SetLimit(s.initWorkers). The variable is not protected by a mutex or atomic operation and is later read after group.Wait() to add a span event. This is a data race and can produce incorrect counts or be flagged by the race detector."
    },
    {
      "file": "pkg/storage/unified/resource/search.go",
      "line": 202,
      "severity": "medium",
      "category": "concurrency",
      "title": "Search watcher goroutine uses background context and does not handle closed channel",
      "body": "The searchSupport.init function starts WatchWriteEvents with watchctx := context.Background() rather than the cancellable ctx passed to init. This watcher goroutine will never be cancelled when the server stops, causing a goroutine leak. Additionally, the goroutine reads from the events channel without checking for closure; if the channel is closed (e.g., due to backend termination), the receive yields a nil *WrittenEvent, and handleEvent will dereference it in the slices.Contains call, causing a panic. The context should be tied to the server and the channel closure should be handled safely."
    },
    {
      "file": "pkg/storage/unified/resource/search.go",
      "line": 202,
      "severity": "medium",
      "category": "data",
      "title": "Gap between index build and watch start can miss write events",
      "body": "In searchSupport.init, the index is built from a snapshot using ListIterator (lines 181-193), and only afterwards is WatchWriteEvents called to start the watcher (line 203). Any writes that occur between the snapshot read and the watcher's initialization will not be reflected in the newly built index, because the watcher starts after the build and does not replay missed events. This can lead to stale search results until the next event for that resource. The watcher should ideally be started before or atomically with the snapshot, or the backend should provide a mechanism to replay missed events."
    }
  ]
}

findings.title: Concurrent BuildIndex for the same key can cause file index creation errors
findings.body: Removing the global cacheMu.Lock from BuildIndex means two goroutines can now concurrently build an index for the same NamespacedResource. getOrCreateIndex does not provide per-key mutual exclusion (see TODO at resource/search.go lines 288-290), so concurrent search requests for the same resource will both see a nil index and call BuildIndex. For file-based indexes (size > FileThreshold), both goroutines will call bleve.New on the same directory path, which is not safe and can fail with an error such as 'index already exists' or corrupt the index. For memory indexes, both will build identical indexes and the last insertion wins, wasting work. Need per-key locking or singleflight to prevent duplicate concurrent builds.

findings.title: TotalDocs reads the cache map without holding RLock
findings.body: TotalDocs iterates over b.cache without acquiring b.cacheMu.RLock. With the reduced locking in BuildIndex, cache is now written concurrently by any call to BuildIndex (e.g., from getOrCreateIndex on search requests) while TotalDocs may be called (for example, in searchSupport.init at resource/search.go line 216 or externally). This constitutes a concurrent map read/write and will cause a runtime panic or map corruption. TotalDocs must take cacheMu.RLock, or the cache must be otherwise synchronized.

findings.title: Cancel function not called when Init fails during NewResourceServer
findings.body: NewResourceServer creates a cancellable context and stores its cancel function in the server struct. If s.Init(ctx) returns an error, the function logs and returns nil, err without calling s.cancel(). Any goroutines started during Init (e.g., from lifecycle.Init or WatchWriteEvents in search.init) may continue running with no way to be stopped, leaking resources. The cancel should be invoked before returning the error.

findings.title: Data race on totalBatchesIndexed in concurrent errgroup goroutines
findings.body: Inside s.init, totalBatchesIndexed++ is executed by multiple goroutines running under an errgroup with SetLimit(s.initWorkers). The variable is not protected by a mutex or atomic operation and is later read after group.Wait() to add a span event. This is a data race and can produce incorrect counts or be flagged by the race detector.

findings.title: Search watcher goroutine uses background context and does not handle closed channel
findings.body: The searchSupport.init function starts WatchWriteEvents with watchctx := context.Background() rather than the cancellable ctx passed to init. This watcher goroutine will never be cancelled when the server stops, causing a goroutine leak. Additionally, the goroutine reads from the events channel without checking for closure; if the channel is closed (e.g., due to backend termination), the receive yields a nil *WrittenEvent, and handleEvent will dereference it in the slices.Contains call, causing a panic. The context should be tied to the server and the channel closure should be handled safely.

findings.title: Gap between index build and watch start can miss write events
findings.body: In searchSupport.init, the index is built from a snapshot using ListIterator (lines 181-193), and only afterwards is WatchWriteEvents called to start the watcher (line 203). Any writes that occur between the snapshot read and the watcher's initialization will not be reflected in the newly built index, because the watcher starts after the build and does not replay missed events. This can lead to stale search results until the next event for that resource. The watcher should ideally be started before or atomically with the snapshot, or the backend should provide a mechanism to replay missed events.
